core_meaning.primary_meaning: Haneef corresponds to the Arabic form حنيف and is glossed in this record as “One who inclines to pure monotheism, a true monotheist.” The record associates the form with root ح ن ف (ḥ-n-f). The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: One who inclines to pure monotheism, a true monotheist
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Haneef corresponds to the Arabic form حنيف (Arabic root ح ن ف (ḥ-n-f); حَنِيف (Ḥanīf)). Its core sense is monotheist; one who inclines to pure worship of god. Haneef is Arabic حَنِيف (Ḥanīf) 'one who inclines to pure monotheism, a true monotheist', from the root ح ن ف (ḥ-n-f). The word appears in the Qur'an. The source gloss 'gracious, generous, kind' is unsupported and belongs to a different root; it has been replaced with the lexical sense. Same name as hanif.
